Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

CEREMONIAL
Mayor Rocha presented a Certificate of Recognition to Ms. Elvira Lopez in honor of her being chosen as the 2009 Outstanding School Crossing guard of the Year for the City of Azusa. Mr. Tony Contreras and the City Council presented Ms. Lopez with the flowers.
Councilmember Gonzales presented a Proclamation from the Mayor of Seal Beach, to Maricela Cuevas in recognition of Azusa Beautiful participation in Save Our Beach Campaign.
A.
PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
Mr. Paul Miller, apartment building owner, addressed Council regarding charges for business tax. He compared tax with surrounding cities, asked for clarification on the term tax or a license, stated they should be in line with other communities, commented on the 20% late fee.
Mr. Mike Lee wished all a happy Cinco de Mayo and Mother’s Day, reminded all to vote in election, announced debate at Baldwin Park Senior Center, 7 p.m., and announced Post Office food drive, Saturday, May 9th.
Mr. Glen Kennedy addressed Council presenting his volunteer graffiti program and requested that he be allowed to work in the City of Azusa; he responded to questions posed by Council regarding his program.
Mr. Gustavo Aguirre announced a fund raiser for Aids Lifecycle, the battle against HIV and aids. He stated that he will be riding his bicycle this week end to raies funds, he provided statistics, i.e. dates and research regarding the disease; his goal is to raise $3,000 by May 30th.
Pastor Samuel Martinez President of the Azusa Ministerial Association made the following anncements: Annual National Day of Prayer, Thursday, May 7th at 7 p.m. at the First Presbyterian Church at the corner of Soldano and Foothill and Mayor’s Prayer Breakfast on May 20th, at Azusa Pacific University at 7:30 a.m. For question and to purchase tickets call 991-8251.
Ms. Virginia Brown addressed Council in opposition to the agenda item requesting authorization to solict request for (RFP) for Azusa Transit Operations and Fleet Services. She praised the Azusa Dial A Ride Services stating the buses are clean and safe, drivers are courteous and helpful. She noted the negative aspects of contract drivers and talked about bad experiences she has had with other types of public transportation.
Ms. Paula Mitton and Josephine Gehring addressed Council in favor of the current Dial a Ride Service; they read letter into record requesting that Dial a Ride not be changed and talked about the advantages of it. They submitted the letter with signatures attached requesting that the current service remain.
Ms. Carolyn Crawford addressed Council in favor of the current Azusa Transportation Program and spoke about its benefits and expressed concern about possible decrease in senior services if there is a change.
Ms. Joan Helvey addressed Council thanking all who are supporting the department, she detailed the history of the dial a ride program and its growth as well as the need of the residents who are transported, she noted the personal care given by the drivers and office staff.
Mr. Mike Gaston representing Azusa City Employees Association, addressed Council expressing his concern about contracting out the Azusa Transportation Department. He talked about the benefits of the programs and urged Council to consider the human factor and not put out the Request For Proposals.
Mr. Joe Guarrera addressed Council and talked about the personal care the drivers provide and about another time in 80’s when the services were contracted out and the negative outcome. He talked about Prop A and Prop C funds and what they covered when he adminstered the program. He talked about the importance of training and requesterd the item be tabled.
Mr. Carlos Guido, Azusa Transportation driver addressed Council regarding the RFP and read a memo into the record regarding the proposed action and the benefits and quality of the current program to residents. He introduced the employees being affected by the proposed action and requested to give the proposal more thought.
City Attorney Carvalho responded to question from Paul Miller regarding the fee vs tax. She stated that it is a tax and detailed how it came about in the 80’s. City Manager Delach responded the question from Glen Kennedy stating that he and the Director of Public Works would meet with him. Mayor Rocha announced that there will be brochures on the back table left by Mr. Aguirre.
Ms. Yvonne Lee addressed Council and expressed her opposition to contracting out Azusa Transit and praised the loyalty of the current employees and asked to find other ways to save money. Talked about the human aspect which should be taken into consideration.
Mr. Bob Donnelson addressed Council and thanked city for supporting Relay For Life; noted and thanked staff members and Council members who participated in the event. He gave a special thanks to VFW and Azusa Veterans Committee for recognizing his son in -law, Staff Sergeant Nicholas Dospital who received a Bronze Star Medal.
Azusa City Clerk Mendoza advised that she received three letters in support of of the Azusa Transportation Program from Robert Jensen, Paula Milker, Charlotte Morgan, and Councilmember Hanks advised that he received a phone call from Doreen Kaufman in favor of the program.
City Manager Delach responsed to Azusa Transit issue stating that staff approached the issue with compassion and the purpose was to see if there would be cost savings. He talked about the high cost of workers compensation claims in this department and felt it was important to bring it to Councils attention.
B.
REPORTS, UPDATES, AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL
City Manager Delach announced that Assemblyman Dr. Ed Hernandez will be at the Azusa Senior Center on Saturday, May 9th at 9:30 a.m. providing an update on voter approved Measure R which may fund the upcoming Gold Line.
1.
Mayor Rocha - request for proclamation for Alan Thorndike in honor of his retirement from the Azusa Unified School District.
Moved by Councilmember Gonzales, seconded by Councilmember Carrillo and unanimously carried to approve request for proclamation for Alan Thorndike in honor of his retirement from the Azusa Unified School District.
2.
Request by Staff for a proclamation to proclaim the week of May 17th - 23rd as American Public Works Week, in the City of Azusa.
Moved by Councilmember Hanks, seconded by Mayor Pro-Tem Macias and unanimously carried to approve proclamation to proclaim the week of May 17th - 23rd as American Public Works Week, in the City of Azusa.
3.
Mayor Rocha - request for proclamation for First Sergeant John B. Wood of the National Guard Armory in honor of his retirement.
Moved by Mayor Rocha, seconded by Councilmember Carrillo and unanimously carried to approve request for proclamation for First Sergeant John B. Wood of the National Guard Armory in honor of his retirement.
Mayor Pro-Tem Macias thanked all who spoke regarding the Azusa Transit Dial a Ride and wished all a Happy Mother’s Day.
Councilmember Hanks wished all a Happy Mother's Day.
Councilmember Gonzales wished all a Happy Mother's Day.
Councilmember Carrillo thanked all for comments in support of the Azusa Transit Dial a Ride; he congratulated Parks and Recreation Department for the sucess of the Cinco de Mayo celebration; all who were involved in the Relay For Life Event and wished Happy Mother’s Day to his wife, mother and all others in the community.
Mayor Rocha wished all a Happy Mother’s Day and announced the following: Sunday, May 10, 9:00 a.m., Mother’s Day Event; the hanging of yellow ribbons in front of the Veterans Memorial Monuments and continental breakfast following; re-hanging three new banners on Azusa Avenue for Leroy Harris Kelly and two others; thanks to organizers in the Relay for Life and Cinco de Mayo event; relayed a message regarding bus service, his Mom and friends.

D-8 RFP Azusa Transit
SPECIAL CALL ITEM: Mayor Pro-Tem Macias addressed this item stating that he researched this issue and found that it works well at this time, the quality of service is good, the transportation program works well and he is not in favor of seeking request for proposals.
Councilmember Gonzales concurred with Mayor Pro-Tem Macias, stating that there are twelve employees in the Azusa Transit Program and there is no guarantee that they will retain their jobs if the service is contract out. He thanked staff for looking into the issue, but the employess are loyal to the City and he received over 50 phone calls confirming that. He expressed his opposition to the RFP.
Mayor Rocha read portions of the contract aloud; expressed his sentiments to the drivers and employees, and expressed his opposition to the RFP stating there is no need for it.
Councilmember Hanks addressed the issue acknowledging the phone calls he received from residents and asked staff what the future of the gas tax was. Director of Public Works Haes responded stating that there will be approximately $330,000 less in than last year. City Manager Delach stated that Prop C money can also be used to pave major thorough fares, there are potential savings and staff was just looking into the feasibility. Councilmember Hanks expressed appreciation to staff for the report and asked about workers compensation which the City Manager advised was very high. Discussion was held regarding safety training, appreciation to staff, desire to reduce expenses here and maintain level of service.
Councilmember Carrillo praised staff for the work they did on this project in looking for savings and trying to provide further services to residents. He read from the RFP about the level of services and the offer of jobs to current employees.
City Manager Delach talked about the implications from some and rumors that they have no compassion, but he and staff do embrace what the community and have concern and care for them.
